newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-HODDLE PRAISES SCHOLES AFTER OUTSTANDING DEBUT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-HODDLE PRAISES SCHOLES AFTER OUTSTANDING DEBUT.

text.p: Paul Scholes enjoyed a superb full international debut against Italy in the Tournoi de France on Wednesday, scoring one goal and making the other in England's 2-0 win.
"He played very well and showed a lot of maturity for a young player," said his delighted manager Glenn Hoddle.

"Ever since he has joined the England squad, he has looked at home with the rest of the players...We changed the system today with Ian Wright playing alone up front and Paul playing in midfield with Teddy Sheringham.
"It worked well for him because he is a natural goalscorer and can come forwrd to score when he gets the chance."

Scholes, who made his first senior appearance for England for the final 25 minutes against South Africa last month, provided the final pass to end the move which set up Ian Wright for the opening goal opener after 26 minutes.

A minute before halftime Wright returned the compliment, passing to Scholes who burst away from defender Antonio Benarrivo 12 metres from goal. He then turned to lash home a left-foot volley which gave Italian goalkeeper Angelo Peruzzi no chance.

He was involved in many of England's build-ups and was one of a Manchester United phalanx in the team which included David Beckham, Gary and Phil Neville, and former United team mate Paul Ince, as well as late substitute Andy Cole.
Between them they controlled almost all the first half and much of the second as England chalked up their first win over Italy since November 1977.

"Beckham, Scholes and Phil Neville had lots of possesion and created lots of opportunities," said Hoddle. There has been a lot of voices calling for Beckham to play in the centre of midfield and I was very pleased with the way he performed there."
England, fresh from beating Poland 2-0 in a World Cup qualifier in Chorzow on Saturday, showed six changes from that side for their opening match of this tournament.
But they impressed with teamwork, confidence and no lack of flair against 10 of the side that beat them 1-0 in a World Cup qualifier in London in February.
The two sides meet again in their final World Cup qualifier in Rome in October when the automatic qualifer from their group for France '98 will be decided.
Although this result will have no bearing on that match, Italian coach Cesare Maldini could not hide his disappointment with his team's performance.
"It was end-of-season stuff from us, we did not play well and England did. But we made too many mistakes and paid a high price for them. Then we didn't make the best of the chances we did create
"I will change the team for the match against Brazil on Sunday."

Italy's best chance came on the stroke of halftime when Dino Baggio controlled Gianfranco Zola's free kick and sent a fierce drive straight at England goalkeeper Tim Flowers who was unable to hold the shot. The ball eventually bounced back to Zola but he shot wide.

England's next match is against France in Montpellier on Saturday while the Italians play Brazil in Lyon on Sunday -- their first meeting since Brazil beat them on penalties in the 1994 World Cup final.
